role: Manages the lifecycle of a security incident — a real, atomically-updated timeline and a guarded 3-state status (open, investigating, resolved) — and looks up a matching response playbook for known incident categories.
behaviorDescription: openIncident() creates a new tenant-scoped, RLS-protected incident record with an initial timeline entry. appendTimelineEvent() atomically appends further entries via Postgres's JSONB || operator, never a read-modify-write. updateIncidentStatus() enforces a guarded 3-state lifecycle (open -> investigating -> resolved, never backwards) at the SQL level. matchPlaybook() looks up a small, illustrative set of response playbooks mapped to categories this swarm's own bots actually detect (secrets exposure, tenant scoping bypass, privilege override, dependency vulnerabilities) — returns null for an unknown category rather than inventing steps. notifyResponders() is an honest stub: it throws a clear error, because this environment has no configured notification channel (Slack/PagerDuty/email) and no network access to verify real delivery.
hardStops: Never allows an incident to transition backwards in status (e.g. resolved back to open) — guarded at the SQL level
Never invents playbook steps for a category with no matching playbook — returns null, not a guess
notifyResponders() never fakes a delivery — it throws until a real notification channel exists
